category_title: Aboriginal adolescents in alternative education who resist traditional pedagogy but engage with digital multiliteracies
minimal_context: The student is assigned to independently read a textbook chapter and complete comprehension and grammar worksheets in an alternative education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please read the next chapter in your textbook on your own, answer the comprehension questions, and complete the grammar worksheet.

STUDENT: I'm tired and I don't care about the novel. (Gets up and wanders to one of the classroom computers to watch video clips on YouTube)

TUTOR: You need to finish your independent work right now.

STUDENT: I prefer learning how to locate information on the Internet, read, make notes, and write about guns, gangs, and drugs rather than reading the stories in the textbooks and answering comprehension questions.

TUTOR: We are doing the textbook questions today. Please go back to your desk.

STUDENT: (Interrupting and challenging the teacher) I'm not complying with this. (Walks out of the classroom)

options.A: Institute a classroom norm of assigning a different colored post-it to each student to use while they are independently reading the assigned textbook chapter.
options.B: Involve the student directly in developing and adjusting the assessment rubric for the comprehension and grammar worksheets early on in the current instructional unit.
options.C: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level comprehension questions on the assigned independent worksheet based specifically on the student's current independent reading level.
options.D: Mediate learning through stories, observation and imitation, community support, scaffolding, visual sensory modes, direct statements, group work, and relevant curricula that include the student's lived experiences.
